title: Conditional Sentences: Introduction
content:
## Conditional Sentences: Introduction

Understand the conditional clause and the main clause.

### Lesson focus

1. If it rains, we shall get wet.
2. An if-clause introduces a condition; distinguish it from time clauses and precautions introduced by other expressions.

### Understand the pattern

A conditional sentence connects a condition with a consequence. If normally introduces the condition. Other expressions need different interpretations: unless means if not, provided that sets a requirement, and in case commonly expresses a precaution. Time clauses with when or until are not interchangeable with every if-clause.

### Worked answers and explanation

If it rains, we will get wet has a condition and a possible result. 'Take an umbrella in case it rains' instead explains a precaution taken before knowing whether it will rain. Replacing in case with if changes when and why the umbrella is taken.

### Try another

Rewrite with the condition second: If you practise, your confidence will grow.

### Suggested answer

Your confidence will grow if you practise. The meaning stays the same; a comma is normally unnecessary before the final if-clause.
